observations: Matched V9/V10 1800px street cameras use identical lens, position, lighting and exposure. Limewash now has visible broad mineral variation; the neighbor walls no longer resolve as uniform plain colors.

The facade close-up retains fine photographed plaster grain, with broader warm/cool replastering and restrained sill runoff. Four-kilopixel main and two-kilopixel neighbor bakes preserve a true 1m fine scan repeat.
Three shared-vertex skins carry authored 0.7-4mm relief with genuine rectangular apertures; native reopening and actual GLB geometry inspection verify retained UVs and openings.
Oak grain and separate honed/cut stone finishes remain coherent in the counter and interior views; owned cardinal counter views remain source-bound.
Actual Godot import/capture retains baked wall images, UV scales/offsets and shading data. The overview visibly carries facade variation under separate engine lighting.

comparison_crop.processing: Unchanged RGB crops plus labels; no exposure, grading, sharpening or selective adjustments.

limitations: Only the cafe and two adjoining street frontages are revised. This is not a whole-town migration or rebuilt playable game.
Neighbor sides, shutters/canvas and other context remain simplified. Upstairs/back-of-house/service interiors, physics/navigation and performance validation remain outside this pilot.
The normal contains full authored relief in addition to coarse mesh relief; normal strength .7 is a restrained compromise, not a residual-normal bake. Height scale is artist-authored, not measured.
Small roof/shadow aliasing remains in the GL Compatibility overview. Blender AgX and Godot use different lighting/tone responses; renderer/art parity is not established.
The earlier full-precision model experiment was interrupted by an unexpected host reboot at7/50steps. No generated model texture is used and the Vulkan setup remains quarantined.
User aesthetic acceptance remains open; file, geometry and engine checks do not establish concept-image parity.
